title: COCOANUT -CASES
ingredients: 1 lb. powdered sugar.  1/2 " grated cocoanut.   Whites of 5 egg.   Whip the eggs as for icing, adding the sugar as you go on until it will stand alone, then beat in the cocoanut.
1/2 lb. flour.  2 lemons.  Beat whites and yolks separately; add to all the yolks and the whites of seven eggs the sugar, the rind of two lemons and juice of one. Bake as Fur jelly-cake.

3 cups sugar.  1 cup butter.  1/2 " sweet milk.  Whites of ten eggs.  1/2 teaspoonful soda. } 1 &#160; " &#160; cream-tartar, }sifted with the flour.  4 1/2 cups flour.  Flavor with essence of bitter almond.  Icing, whites of 3 eggs, 1 lb, powdered sugar. Flavor with lemon-juice. Bake in jelly-cake tins, and fill with grated cocoanut, sweetened with a quarter of its weight or powdered sugar, or with icing such as is made for Lee cake, only flavored with lemon entirely.
1 lb. sugar.  1/2 " butter.  1 " currants, washed clean and dredged with flour.  3 cups flour.  4 eggs.  Nutmeg and cinnamon to taste. 1/2 teaspoonful soda dissolved in three tablespoonfuls milk.
instructions: 1 cocoanut, carefully skinned and grated.  Milk of the same. 1 1/2 lb. powdered sugar.  As much water as you have cocoanut milk.  Whites of three eggs.  Dissolve one pound of sugar in the milk and water, Stew until it becomes a "ropy" syrup, and turn out into a buttered dish. Have ready the beaten white of egg, with the remaining half-pound of sugar whipped into it, mix with this the grated cocoanut, and little by little, beating all the while the boiled syrup, so soon as it cools sufficiently not to scald the eggs. Drop in tablespoonfuls upon buttered papers. Try one first, and if it runs, beat in more sugar. Bake in a very moderate oven, watching to prevent scorching. They should not be suffered to brown at all.
These will keep some time, but are best quite fresh.
Mould the mixture with your hands into small cones, and set these far enough apart not to touch one another upon buttered paper in a baking-pan, Bake in a very moderate oven.

To the whites of three eggs allow a pound and a quarter of powdered sugar; beat stiff as for icing, take out enough to cover the top of the cake and set aside. Add to the rest the juice and half the grated rind of a large orange. When the cake is nearly cold, spread this between the layers. Beat into the icing reserved for the top a little lemon-juice, and, if needed, more sugar. It should be stiffer than that spread between the cakes.
